driver.note: baseline is pre-existing desktop/OS GPU usage (Xorg/KDE/Firefox) measured with nvidia-smi immediately before this process started, no training process running; 'raw' is nvidia-smi's system-wide memory.used peak sampled every 0.5s over the whole run (64 samples), 'training_attributable_peak_mib' subtracts the baseline. The last 10 consecutive samples before the run ended sit at 20,845-20,883 MiB, so the peak is a sustained plateau during the load-bearing training steps, not a one-sample outlier.

fits_rationale: Unlike the chunk=2048 re-probe (batch1280-chunked-summary.json), EVERY metric clears the task's own fits formula (peak <= 23,028 - 2,048 = 20,980 MiB) at chunk=512: torch's own peaks (allocated 19,079.7 / reserved 19,444.0, margin 1,536-1,900 MiB) and, this time, the driver-observed peak too (20,883 MiB raw, margin 97 MiB; 19,826 MiB training-attributable, margin 1,154 MiB). The margin on the driver-raw reading is narrow (97 MiB) but positive, on 64 samples sampled at 0.5s with the peak sustained across the last 10 consecutive samples (20,845-20,883 MiB), not a transient spike.

launch_criterion_20260903_task.note: the pre-registered W4 memory launch task's own explicit go/no-go criterion (raw driver peak <= 22,000 MiB, leaving >= 1,028 MiB of the 23,028 MiB card below the ceiling with the desktop baseline included) -- looser than, and in addition to, the general fits_threshold_mib convention above. Both are cleared at chunk=512; chunk=256 was not probed.
